The main takeaway from our work is that

the hole transport parameters in Hg1−xCdxTe with x ≥ 0.5 are predominantly limited by polar optical scattering and ionized-impurity scattering, with the relative strength of these scattering mechanisms being dependent on the CdTe content, the compensation ratio, and the sample temperature.

hole transport in Hg1−xCdxTe films can be adequately modeled using a single scattering mechanism, and that ionized impurities and polar optical phonons are the most important scattering mechanisms in p-type HgCdTe with x ≥ 0.5.
hole mobilities in Hg1-x CdxTe layers can be significantly improved by reducing the arsenic doping level and/or by increasing the CdTe mole fractions.
